questions.q: What is the main risk of defining "win rate" separately inside each dashboard?
options: Dashboards will refuse to load
Different teams may define it differently and report conflicting numbers
Win rate cannot be calculated in a dashboard
It forces every dashboard to use the same colors
questions.explain: Metric drift happens when each builder re-creates a definition slightly differently. A central definition gives everyone one meaning.

questions.q: Which set of fields makes a metric definition precise enough for two analysts to reproduce it?
options: The metric name and a chart type
The owner's name and the dashboard color
The business name only
The aggregation, filters, time basis, and exclusions
questions.explain: Without the filters, time basis, and exclusions, two people can compute different values from the same data and both think they are right.

questions.q: In the capstone's definitions, which is excluded from the Win Rate calculation?
options: Renewal opportunities
Closed Lost opportunities
Opportunities in the Americas
Opportunities older than one day
questions.explain: Win Rate is closed won count divided by all closed count over the trailing four quarters, excluding renewals, so renewals do not inflate it.

options: A test of whether a dataset has an even number of rows
A check that a security predicate blocks all users
A speed test of dashboard load time
A check that a dashboard tile and the central metric show the same value for the same period
questions.explain: Because the dashboard and the semantic model can define the same number separately, a parity test proves they agree and catches drift early.

questions.q: Why does each metric get a named business owner?
options: So one accountable team approves the definition and any changes to it
So the owner can hide the metric from other teams
Because Salesforce will not save a metric without one
So the metric refreshes faster
questions.explain: Ownership creates accountability: the owner approves the definition, certifies it, and signs off on changes recorded in the change log.
